meta.name: AcadSearch Local Benchmark v1.0
meta.description: Controlled local benchmark for reproducible academic search evaluation. Contains 5 domains and 111 real papers with human-curated metadata.

papers.title: A Survey of Hallucination in Large Language Models: Principles, Taxonomy, Challenges, and Open Questions
papers.abstract: Comprehensive survey of hallucination in LLMs including taxonomy, detection methods, mitigation strategies, and evaluation benchmarks.

papers.title: SelfCheckGPT: Zero-Resource Black-Box Hallucination Detection for Generative Large Language Models
papers.abstract: A sampling-based approach to fact-check LLM outputs without external resources, using consistency across multiple sampled responses.

papers.title: DoLa: Decoding by Contrasting Layers Improves Factuality in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: A simple decoding strategy that contrasts logits from later vs earlier transformer layers to reduce hallucinations.

papers.title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
papers.abstract: A benchmark to measure whether a language model is truthful in generating answers, evaluating hallucination and factuality.

papers.title: HaluEval: A Large-Scale Hallucination Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: A comprehensive benchmark with 35K hallucinated and normal samples for evaluating LLM hallucination across multiple tasks.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.abstract: Introduces RAG, combining retrieval with generation to reduce hallucination in knowledge-intensive tasks.

papers.title: FELM: Benchmarking Factuality Evaluation of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: A benchmark for evaluating factuality of LLM outputs across multiple domains including science, history, and common knowledge.

papers.title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
papers.abstract: Augments language model pre-training with a knowledge retriever, enabling the model to retrieve and attend over documents.

papers.title: LM vs LM: Detecting Factual Errors via Cross Examination
papers.abstract: A factuality detection method that uses a secondary LM to cross-examine the primary LM's outputs.

papers.title: Hallucination in Large Language Models: A Systematic Survey
papers.abstract: Systematic survey categorizing hallucination sources, detection methods, and mitigation strategies.

papers.title: Factual Consistency Checking for Abstractive Summarization
papers.abstract: We introduce a natural language inference-based model to detect factual inconsistencies between a document and its summary.

papers.title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems
papers.abstract: We train verifiers to judge the correctness of model-generated solutions to math problems, reducing hallucination in reasoning tasks.

papers.title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Large Language Models via Self-Reflection
papers.abstract: We propose a self-reflection framework where the LLM generates and then critiques its own outputs to reduce factual errors.

papers.title: Detecting Hallucinated Content in Conditional Neural Sequence Generation
papers.abstract: We propose a detection method based on examining the model's internal attention and uncertainty to identify hallucinated spans.

papers.title: RARR: Researching and Revising What Language Models Say, Using Language Models
papers.abstract: We propose a system that uses retrieval to fact-check and revise LLM outputs, reducing hallucination by grounding in external knowledge.

papers.title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long-Form Text Generation
papers.abstract: We propose a fine-grained evaluation metric that decomposes generated text into atomic facts and verifies each against a knowledge source.

papers.title: Do Language Models Know When They Don't Know?
papers.abstract: We study the calibration of LLMs and propose methods to detect when models are likely to hallucinate based on their internal uncertainty.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Without Prompting
papers.abstract: We show that LLMs can self-correct hallucinations by generating and evaluating multiple reasoning chains without explicit prompting.

papers.title: Knowledge-Augmented Language Model Verification
papers.abstract: We propose a verification framework that retrieves relevant knowledge and uses it to verify the factual correctness of LLM outputs.

papers.title: Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models with Contrastive Decoding
papers.abstract: We propose a contrastive decoding method that amplifies differences between a base model and an expert model to detect hallucinated tokens.

papers.title: Improving Factuality in Abstractive Summarization via Fact-Consistency Training
papers.abstract: We propose a training method that uses fact-consistency rewards to fine-tune summarization models, reducing hallucination.

papers.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
papers.abstract: We introduce a framework where an LLM learns to retrieve relevant passages, generate responses, and critique its own outputs to improve factuality.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.abstract: Presents high-quality image generation using diffusion probabilistic models, establishing the foundation for modern diffusion approaches.

papers.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Introduces latent diffusion models (Stable Diffusion), applying diffusion in latent space for efficient high-resolution image synthesis.

papers.title: Adding Conditional Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models (ControlNet)
papers.abstract: Introduces ControlNet, enabling spatial conditioning for text-to-image diffusion models through trainable copies of network blocks.

papers.title: Consistency Models
papers.abstract: A new family of generative models that support fast one-step generation while maintaining sample quality comparable to diffusion models.

papers.title: DPM-Solver: A Fast ODE Solver for Diffusion Probabilistic Model Sampling in Around 10 Steps
papers.abstract: A fast dedicated solver for diffusion ODEs that achieves high-quality samples in about 10 steps, significantly accelerating diffusion sampling.

papers.title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers (DiT)
papers.abstract: Replaces the U-Net backbone with a transformer architecture, demonstrating scalable diffusion models with improved performance.

papers.title: DreamBooth: Fine Tuning Text-to-Image Diffusion Models for Subject-Driven Generation
papers.abstract: A method to personalize text-to-image diffusion models using a few images of a subject, enabling subject-driven generation.

papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Introduces Low-Rank Adaptation, an efficient fine-tuning method widely adopted for diffusion model personalization.

papers.title: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion Models for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
papers.abstract: An improved version of Stable Diffusion with larger architectures, better conditioning, and higher resolution generation.

papers.title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
papers.abstract: A simple and general framework for training generative models using continuous normalizing flows and optimal transport.

papers.title: Improved Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.abstract: We improve denoising diffusion probabilistic models by finding a better noise schedule, reducing the number of steps, and achieving state-of-the-art image generation quality.

papers.title: Diffusion Models Beat GANs on Image Synthesis
papers.abstract: We show that diffusion models can achieve image sample quality superior to the current state-of-the-art generative adversarial networks by improving the architecture and classifier guidance.

papers.title: Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance
papers.abstract: We propose classifier-free guidance, a method for conditioning diffusion models without a separate classifier, by jointly training conditional and unconditional models.

papers.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
papers.abstract: We unify score-based and diffusion models by formulating them as stochastic differential equations, enabling efficient sampling and likelihood computation.

papers.title: Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Generative Models
papers.abstract: We systematically analyze the design space of diffusion models and propose a deterministic sampling method (EDM) that achieves state-of-the-art results.

papers.title: Imagen: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Deep Language Understanding
papers.abstract: We present Imagen, a text-to-image diffusion model leveraging a large language model for text encoding, achieving photorealistic image generation.

papers.title: Progressive Distillation for Fast Sampling of Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: We propose progressive distillation, a method to distill a diffusion model into a model that can generate samples in fewer steps while maintaining quality.

papers.title: Cold Diffusion: Inverting Arbitrary Image Transforms without Noise
papers.abstract: We generalize diffusion models to arbitrary degradation processes (e.g., blur, masking) beyond Gaussian noise, enabling new applications like image restoration.

papers.title: Stable Diffusion: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: We release Stable Diffusion, an open-source latent diffusion model for text-to-image generation, enabling high-resolution synthesis on consumer hardware.

papers.title: GLIDE: Towards Photorealistic Image Generation and Editing with Text-Guided Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: We present GLIDE, a text-guided diffusion model for photorealistic image generation and editing, using classifier-free guidance and CLIP embeddings.

papers.title: DALL-E 2: Hierarchical Text-Conditional Image Generation with CLIP Latents
papers.abstract: We introduce DALL-E 2, a two-stage model that generates images from text descriptions using a prior model and a diffusion decoder, achieving high-quality results.

papers.title: Video Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: We extend diffusion models to video generation by modeling the joint distribution of frames, achieving high-quality video synthesis.

papers.title: Maximum Likelihood Training of Score-Based Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: We show that score-based diffusion models can be trained with maximum likelihood, improving likelihood estimation and sample quality.

papers.title: CodeRL: Mastering Code Generation through Pretrained Models and Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Integrates pretrained language models with deep reinforcement learning for program synthesis, framing code generation as an RL task.

papers.title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback (InstructGPT)
papers.abstract: Trains language models to follow instructions using RLHF, with significant improvements for code generation tasks.

papers.title: Enhancing Code LLMs with Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation: A Survey
papers.abstract: A comprehensive survey of reinforcement learning methods applied to code generation with LLMs, covering RLHF, PPO, and reward design.

papers.title: PPOCoder: Execution-based Code Generation using Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Uses PPO with compiler feedback as reward signal for generating functionally correct code, bridging RL and execution-based verification.

papers.title: RLTF: Reinforcement Learning from Unit Test Feedback
papers.abstract: Proposes using unit test pass rate as a reward signal for fine-tuning code generation models with RL.

papers.title: AlphaCode: Competition-Level Code Generation with Transformer-Based Architectures
papers.abstract: Generates code at competitive programming level using large-scale transformer models with filtering and clustering.

papers.title: CompilerGym: Robust, Performant Compiler Optimization Environments for AI Research
papers.abstract: A reinforcement learning environment for compiler optimization, providing standardized benchmarks for RL-based compiler tuning.

papers.title: Execution-Based Code Generation using Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: A method that uses execution results as a sparse reward signal for training code generation models with RL.

papers.title: Let's Verify Step by Step
papers.abstract: Shows process-supervised reward models outperform outcome supervision for mathematical reasoning, applicable to code generation verification.

papers.title: RL4Fuzz: Reinforcement Learning for Fuzzing
papers.abstract: Applies reinforcement learning to guide fuzzing-based test generation for software, demonstrating RL in code-related optimization.

papers.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
papers.abstract: This paper introduces InstructGPT, a model fine-tuned with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to better align language models with user intent across a wide range of tasks.

papers.title: Competition-level code generation with AlphaCode
papers.abstract: AlphaCode uses transformer-based architectures and large-scale sampling with filtering to solve competitive programming problems at a level comparable to human competitors.

papers.title: RLHF: Reinforcement learning from human feedback
papers.abstract: This paper presents a general method for fine-tuning language models using human preferences as a reward signal, enabling alignment with complex human values.

papers.title: Execution-guided neural program synthesis
papers.abstract: This work proposes a neural program synthesis approach that leverages execution traces to guide the search for correct programs, significantly improving synthesis accuracy.

papers.title: CodeBERT: A pre-trained model for programming and natural languages
papers.abstract: CodeBERT is a bimodal pre-trained model for natural language and programming language, supporting tasks like code search and code documentation generation.

papers.title: Learning to summarize from human feedback
papers.abstract: This paper applies reinforcement learning from human feedback to train a summarization model that produces summaries preferred by human evaluators over those from supervised fine-tuning.

papers.title: Program synthesis with large language models
papers.abstract: This paper explores the use of large language models for program synthesis, demonstrating that scaling model size and using execution-based filtering significantly improves performance on the MBPP benchmark.

papers.title: Self-consistency improves chain of thought reasoning in language models
papers.abstract: Self-consistency generates multiple reasoning paths and selects the most consistent answer, improving chain-of-thought reasoning in language models without additional training.

papers.title: CodeGen: An open large language model for code with multi-turn program synthesis
papers.abstract: CodeGen is a family of large language models for code generation, trained on a multi-turn program synthesis dataset and showing strong performance on the HumanEval benchmark.

papers.title: Direct preference optimization: Your language model is secretly a reward model
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) simplifies RLHF by directly optimizing language model policies from human preferences without explicit reward modeling.

papers.title: CodeT5: Identifier-aware unified pre-trained encoder-decoder models for code understanding and generation
papers.abstract: CodeT5 is a unified pre-trained encoder-decoder model for code that leverages identifier-aware objectives to improve performance on both code understanding and generation tasks.

papers.title: Constrained language models yield few-shot semantic parsers
papers.abstract: This paper proposes constrained decoding for language models to generate valid programs in few-shot semantic parsing, improving accuracy without additional training.

papers.title: Improving language models by retrieving from trillions of tokens
papers.abstract: RETRO introduces retrieval-augmented language models that access a large external memory, improving perplexity and generation quality by leveraging trillions of tokens.

papers.title: Codex: Evaluating large language models trained on code
papers.abstract: Codex is a GPT-based model fine-tuned on code from GitHub, evaluated on the HumanEval benchmark, demonstrating strong capability in generating functionally correct code from docstrings.

papers.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision (CLIP)
papers.abstract: Trains a vision model using natural language supervision at scale, achieving strong zero-shot transfer across many vision tasks.

papers.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Efficiently leverages frozen pre-trained image encoders and LLMs with a lightweight Q-Former for vision-language tasks.

papers.title: LLaVA: Large Language and Vision Assistant
papers.abstract: An end-to-end trained large multimodal model combining a vision encoder with an LLM for general-purpose visual and language understanding.

papers.title: Align before Fuse: Vision and Language Representation Learning with Momentum Distillation
papers.abstract: Proposes ALBEF for vision-language representation learning with contrastive loss and momentum distillation for better alignment.

papers.title: Flamingo: A Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
papers.abstract: A family of visual language models that achieve strong few-shot performance by interleaving pretrained vision and language models with gated cross-attention.

papers.title: CoCa: Contrastive Captioners are Image-Text Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Unifies contrastive learning and captioning in a single model, achieving strong performance on both alignment and generative tasks.

papers.title: Visual Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: Proposes instruction tuning for multimodal models by converting image-text pairs into instruction-following format.

papers.title: BERT Can See Out of the Box: On the Cross-modal Transferability of Textual Representations
papers.abstract: Investigates how well text-only representations transfer to vision-language tasks, showing surprising cross-modal transfer.

papers.title: SigLIP: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training
papers.abstract: Replaces softmax-based contrastive loss with a simpler sigmoid loss for vision-language pre-training, achieving better performance at scale.

papers.title: ImageBind: One Embedding Space To Bind Them All
papers.abstract: Learns a joint embedding across six modalities (image, text, audio, depth, thermal, IMU), demonstrating emergent cross-modal alignment.

papers.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that a simple pre-training task of predicting which caption goes with which image can learn state-of-the-art image representations that transfer to a wide variety of downstream tasks without any dataset-specific training.

papers.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
papers.abstract: We show that a pure transformer applied directly to sequences of image patches can perform very well on image classification tasks when pre-trained on sufficiently large datasets.

papers.title: BLIP: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training for Unified Vision-Language Understanding and Generation
papers.abstract: We propose BLIP, a new VLP framework which transfers flexibly to both vision-language understanding and generation tasks by bootstrapping captions from noisy web data.

papers.title: Improved Baselines with Momentum Contrastive Learning
papers.abstract: We present a simple modification to MoCo that improves its performance by using a larger queue and a more consistent momentum update, achieving competitive results on ImageNet and downstream tasks.

papers.title: SimCLR: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
papers.abstract: We simplify contrastive representation learning by using a composition of data augmentations and a learnable nonlinear transformation between the representation and the contrastive loss, achieving state-of-the-art results on ImageNet.

papers.title: Scaling Vision Transformers
papers.abstract: We study the scaling behavior of Vision Transformers and show that they can match or outperform ResNets on large-scale image classification tasks with appropriate model size and data.

papers.title: PaLI: A Jointly-Scaled Multilingual Language-Image Model
papers.abstract: We present PaLI, a model that achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple vision-language tasks by jointly scaling the vision and language components to billions of parameters.

papers.title: VinVL: Revisiting Visual Representations in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: We revisit the role of visual representations in vision-language models and propose VinVL, which uses an improved object detection model to extract richer visual features, leading to state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks.

papers.title: Oscar: Object-Semantics Aligned Pre-training for Vision-Language Tasks
papers.abstract: We propose Oscar, a pre-training method that uses object tags as anchor points to align image and text modalities, achieving strong performance on vision-language understanding and generation tasks.

papers.title: UniCLIP: Unified Framework for Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training
papers.abstract: We propose UniCLIP, a unified framework that integrates contrastive learning across multiple modalities and tasks, achieving strong performance on both image-text retrieval and zero-shot classification.

papers.title: Multimodal Few-Shot Learning with Frozen Language Models
papers.abstract: We show that a frozen large language model can be adapted to multimodal few-shot learning by training a vision encoder to map images into the language model's embedding space, enabling strong performance on visual question answering and captioning.

papers.title: Strategies for Pre-training Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Systematic study of strategies for pretraining GNNs, including node-level and graph-level pretraining objectives.

papers.title: Graph Contrastive Learning with Augmentations
papers.abstract: Proposes graph contrastive learning framework with four types of graph data augmentations for self-supervised GNN pretraining.

papers.title: GraphMAE: Self-Supervised Masked Graph Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Applies masked autoencoding to graphs, reconstructing masked node features from the remaining graph structure.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Graph Transformer on Large-Scale Molecular Data
papers.abstract: Applies self-supervised pretraining to graph transformers for molecular property prediction at large scale.

papers.title: BGRL: Bootstrapped Representation Learning on Graphs
papers.abstract: A self-supervised graph representation method using bootstrapping without negative samples, simpler and more scalable than contrastive methods.

papers.title: GCC: Graph Contrastive Coding for Graph Neural Network Pre-Training
papers.abstract: A self-supervised graph pretraining framework using contrastive learning on subgraph instances.

papers.title: Masked Label Prediction: Unified Message Passing Model for Semi-Supervised Classification
papers.abstract: A unified framework connecting masked reconstruction and label propagation for graph-based semi-supervised learning.

papers.title: GraphLoG: Graph Contrastive Learning with Local-Global Mutual Information Maximization
papers.abstract: Maximizes mutual information between local node representations and global graph representations for self-supervised learning.

papers.title: AutoSSL: Automated Self-Supervised Learning for Graphs
papers.abstract: Automatically searches for the best combination of self-supervised pretext tasks for graph representation learning.

papers.title: SimGRACE: A Simple Framework for Graph Contrastive Learning without Data Augmentation
papers.abstract: A simple graph contrastive learning framework that uses model perturbation instead of data augmentation, reducing computational overhead.

papers.title: When Does Contrastive Learning Preserve Graph Structure?
papers.abstract: Theoretically analyzes the conditions under which graph contrastive learning preserves structural information and proposes a new method (Graph Barlow Twins) based on redundancy reduction.

papers.title: Contrastive Multi-View Representation Learning on Graphs
papers.abstract: Introduces a multi-view contrastive learning framework for graphs that maximizes agreement between different structural views (e.g., node and subgraph levels).

papers.title: InfoGraph: Unsupervised and Semi-supervised Graph-Level Representation Learning via Mutual Information Maximization
papers.abstract: Extends Deep Graph Infomax to graph-level representation learning by maximizing mutual information between graph and substructure representations.

papers.title: Graph Contrastive Learning Automated
papers.abstract: Proposes an automated framework (AutoGCL) that learns graph augmentations and contrastive objectives jointly via bilevel optimization.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Graph Learning with Negative Sampling
papers.abstract: Proposes a self-supervised graph learning method that uses negative sampling to learn node representations by distinguishing positive and negative edges.

papers.title: Graph Barlow Twins: A Redundancy Reduction Approach to Graph Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Applies the Barlow Twins objective to graphs, reducing redundancy between embeddings of different augmented views to learn informative representations.

papers.title: GraphMAE2: A Masked Graph Autoencoder with Graph-Aware Masking and Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Extends GraphMAE with graph-aware masking strategies and multi-scale reconstruction for improved self-supervised graph learning.

papers.title: Graph Contrastive Learning with Adaptive Augmentation
papers.abstract: Introduces adaptive augmentation strategies for graph contrastive learning that adjust augmentation based on graph structure and node features.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Graph Neural Networks via Diverse and Interactive Augmentations
papers.abstract: Proposes a self-supervised framework that uses diverse augmentations and interactive learning between views to improve graph representations.

papers.title: Graph Self-Supervised Learning: A Survey
papers.abstract: Provides a comprehensive survey of graph self-supervised learning methods, including contrastive, generative, and predictive approaches.

papers.title: Bootstrapped Representation Learning on Graphs
papers.abstract: Proposes a bootstrapping approach for graph representation learning that avoids negative samples by using a target network to generate positive pairs.
